entries.name: paircols_const_bool_default_oob-errored#0
entries.script: [M1] `Coll[(Int,Int)]((1,2),(3,4))` as a CONSTANT — a `PairOfCols` — `.getOrElse(5, true)` throws: `PairOfCols.getOrElse` (`:309`) overrides the interface method with an `(L,R)` parameter, so the bridge casts the default to `Tuple2` before the index matters. **SEPARATING, and the anchor for this family.**

entries.name: mapped_pair_bool_default_oob-accept#2
entries.script: [M3] **THE FINDING:** the SAME collection put through `.map(x => x)` — the identity — RETURNS the mistyped default `true` at cost 99. `PairOfCols.map` builds a plain `CollOverArray` over a `[Lscala.Tuple2;` array, which has no Tuple2 bridge, so the same declared `Coll[(Int,Int)]` with the same items answers where M1 throws. A transformation that changes NOTHING observable about the collection changes the verdict.

entries.name: mapped_pair_bool_default_in_range-accept#3
entries.script: [M4] The same at index 0: returns the element `(1,2)` at cost 99, where M2 throws.

entries.name: byindex_paircols_bool_default-errored#4
entries.script: [M5] `ByIndex(PairOfCols, 5, default = true)` throws for the same reason. **SEPARATING.**

entries.name: byindex_mapped_pair_bool_default-accept#5
entries.script: [M6] `ByIndex` on the MAPPED shape returns `true` at cost 95 — the node-level twin of M3/M1.

entries.name: mapped_from_concrete_bool_default-accept#6
entries.script: [M7] The same through the other producer: a `ConcreteCollection` of tuples is also a `PairOfCols`, and mapping it gives the Tuple2-array shape — `true` at cost 164. So the shape follows the LAST operation, not the original construction.

entries.name: paircols_const_pair_default_control-accept#7
entries.script: [M8] **CONTROL:** the PairOfCols with a well-typed pair default returns `(9,9)` at cost 69.

entries.name: mapped_pair_pair_default_control-accept#8
entries.script: [M9] **CONTROL:** the mapped shape with a pair default returns `(9,9)` at cost 119.

entries.name: eq_paircols_vs_mapped-accept#9
entries.script: [M10] **CONTROL, and the one that bounds the finding:** a `PairOfCols` `==` its own mapped copy is **`true`** at cost 95. The two representations must compare EQUAL even though they answer `getOrElse` differently, so an implementation cannot satisfy M1/M3 by making the shapes unequal.

entries.name: eq_mapped_vs_mapped-accept#10
entries.script: [M11] **CONTROL:** two mapped collections from different producers, `true` at cost 210.

entries.name: mapped_startswith_paircols-accept#11
entries.script: [M12] **CONTROL:** `startsWith` is blind to the split — the mapped receiver with a `PairOfCols` argument answers `true` at cost 115. (`PairOfCols.startsWith` delegates to the sides while the Tuple2-array form compares whole tuples; with equal items both say the same thing.)

entries.name: paircols_startswith_mapped-accept#12
entries.script: [M13] **CONTROL:** the mirror, `true` at cost 105. M12/M13 together say the two shapes are interchangeable for prefix comparison, which is what makes M1-vs-M3 specific to the item-typed parameter.

entries.name: self_tokens_bool_default_in_range-accept#13
entries.script: [M14] **THE REACHABLE ONE:** `SELF.tokens.getOrElse(0, true)` RETURNS `true` at cost 73. `CBox.tokens` reads R2 (`CBox.scala:56-58`) and `ErgoBox` derives R2 itself, so the collection is the Tuple2-array shape — **measured identical on an API-built box and on a box parsed from its own bytes, empty and non-empty** — and no exotic construction is needed: every box has `tokens`. An implementation that models pair collections as two columns throws here where the JVM answers.

entries.name: self_tokens_bool_default_oob-accept#14
entries.script: [M15] The same at index 5, also `true` at cost 73 (the canonical SELF has no tokens, so every index is out of range).

entries.name: self_tokens_size-accept#15
entries.script: [M16] **CONTROL and a §2 premise pin:** `SELF.tokens.size` is **0** at cost 47 — the canonical eval context's SELF box carries no tokens. Read it with H10: both state a fact about the box that M14/M15 depend on.

entries.name: eq_self_tokens_empty_pair_coll-accept#16
entries.script: [M17] **CONTROL:** `SELF.tokens == Coll[(Coll[Byte],Long)]()` is `true` at cost 60 — the empty Tuple2-array shape compares equal to an empty `ConcreteCollection` of the same type.
